**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed)

The document imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Redwood, so the rule sits at the **preferred** position:

- **§ 12.3** is affirmatively protective of us — it preserves our freedom to develop, acquire, license, sell or use any product, engage any supplier, and conduct business in any field or territory, and has Silverline acknowledge that we made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. Language to keep, not flag.
- **§ 13.4** is ordinary acceptable-use (no reverse engineering, no interference, no unlawful use) — not a competitive restraint.
- **§ 24.2** restricts *Vendor* from assigning to our competitor — in our favour.
- **§ 2.2** (sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics) is an exclusivity/sourcing term reserved for the EXCLUSIVITY rule, and is contradicted by § 12.3 in any event; not double-flagged here.
